title: Fidel Castaño orders the Los Tangueros paramilitary group to commit the Pueblo Bello Massacre. They loot houses, round up peasants in the town square, select 43 men and boys to kidnap, and torture them. Of the 43 kidnapped, 6 are murdered,…
text: Fidel Antonio Castaño Gil a.k.a. Rambo was a Colombian drug lord and paramilitary who was among the founders of Los Pepes and the Peasant Self-Defense Forces of Cordoba and Uraba (ACCU), a paramilitary group which ultimately became a member of the larger United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia (AUC) from which he became its leader until his death in 1994.

title: Avianca Flight 052: 73 people die after an Avianca plane flying from Medellín to New York City, United States crashes in Cove Neck, New York.
text: Avianca Flight 052 was a regularly scheduled flight from Bogotá, Colombia, to New York City, United States, via Medellín, Colombia, that crashed on January 25, 1990, at 21:34. The Boeing 707 flying this route ran out of fuel after a failed attempt to land at John F. Kennedy International Airport (JFK), causing the aircraft to crash onto a hillside in the small village of Cove Neck, New York, on the north shore of …

title: U.S. president George H. W. Bush, president of Colombia Virgilio Barco, president of Peru Alan García, and president of Bolivia Jaime Paz Zamora attend a summit in Cartagena on combating drug trafficking.
text: George Herbert Walker Bush was the 41st president of the United States, serving from 1989 to 1993. A member of the Republican Party, he served as the 43rd vice president under Ronald Reagan and previously held a multitude of other federal, ambassadorial, and party positions.

title: Journalist Silvia Duzán is assassinated during the Third Cimitarra Massacre in Cimitarra, Santander alongside Josué Vargas, Miguel Ángel Barajas, and Saúl Castañeda.
text: Santander is a department of Colombia. It is located in the central northern part of the country, and borders the Magdalena River to the east, Boyacá to the south and southeast, Norte de Santander to the northeast, Cesar to the north, and the Bolivar and Antioquia Departments to the west.

title: 1990 Colombian parliamentary election.
text: Parliamentary elections were held in Colombia on 11 March 1990 alongside local elections and an unofficial referendum on electing a Constitutional Assembly.

title: Bernardo Jaramillo Ossa is assassinated.
text: Bernardo Jaramillo Ossa was a Colombian politician and member of the Colombian Communist Party. Jaramillo started working primarily in the Urabá Antioquia region until 1987 when he assumed the presidency of the Patriotic Union Party (UP) after the assassination of Jaime Pardo.

title: Carlos Pizarro Leongómez is assassinated.
text: Carlos Pizarro Leongómez was a Colombian guerrilla leader who headed the 19th of April Movement (M-19). Pizarro accepted the demobilization of M-19 that transformed the insurgents into a political party, the M-19 Democratic Alliance (Alianza Democrática M-19) (AD/M-19), but was assassinated on 26 April 1990 while running for president of Colombia.

title: 1990 Colombian presidential election
text: Presidential elections were held in Colombia on 27 May 1990. In an election tarnished by violence, the result was a victory for César Gaviria of the Liberal Party, who received 48.2% of the vote.

title: May 1990 Colombian Constitutional Assembly referendum
text: A referendum on electing a Constitutional Assembly was held in Colombia on 27 May 1990 alongside presidential elections. The proposal was approved by 96% of voters.

title: A formal complaint is filed by Americas Watch with Carla Hills, the US Trade Representative, questioning Colombia's eligibility for trade benefits under the Generalized System of Preferences on the basis of labor rights violations and…
text: Carla Anderson Hills is an American lawyer and former government official. A member of the Republican Party, she previously served as the 5th United States secretary of housing and urban development under President Gerald Ford from 1975 to 1977 and as the 10th United States trade representative under President George H. W. Bush from 1989 to 1993.

title: 13-15 July – 1990 South American Junior Championships in Athletics.
text: The 22nd South American Junior Championships in Athletics were held in Bogotá, Colombia, at the Estadio El Campín from July 13–15, 1990.
wiki: 1990 South American Junior Championships in Athletics

title: The first leg of the 1989 Copa Interamericana is held at Atanasio Girardot in Medellín. Colombia's Atlético Nacional beats México's UNAM 2 to 0.
text: Atanasio Girardot Sports Complex is a sports complex located in Medellín, Colombia. The complex includes Estadio Atanasio Girardot, Medellín Sports Coliseum, Luis Alberto Villegas Stadium, and Alfonso Galvis Duque Stadium.

title: The second leg of the 1989 Copa Interamericana is held at Olímpico Universitario Stadium in Mexico City, México. Colombia's Atlético Nacional beats México's UNAM 4 to 1.
text: The 1989 Copa Interamericana was the 12th. edition of the Copa Interamericana.

title: Los Cocos farm massacre: Armed men in military uniforms kill 26 people playing soccer at a ranch in Candelaria, Valle del Cauca.
text: Valle del Cauca is a department in western Colombia abutting the Pacific Ocean. Its capital is Santiago de Cali.

title: Community leaders from the Aguablanca district of Cali Francisco Sapizábal, Luis Cuazquer, and Jorge Ocampo are “disappeared”. Their bodies are found, shot and tortured, in the Cauca river on the 16th.
text: The Cauca River is a major river in Colombia that lies between the Occidental and Central cordilleras. From its headwaters in southwestern Colombia near the city of Popayán, it flows 965 km (600 mi) until it joins the Magdalena River near Magangué in Bolívar Department, and the combined river flows into the Caribbean Sea with a total length of 1,350 km (840 mi).

title: Miss Colombia 1990 is held in Cartagena; Miss Atlántico Maribel Gutiérrez wins.
text: Atlántico is a department of Colombia in the north of the country, with the Caribbean Sea to its north, the Bolívar Department to its west and south across the Canal del Dique, and the Magdalena Department to its east across the Magdalena River. Despite having the third-smallest area among Colombia's thirty-two departments, it is the fifth-largest by population with 2,535,517.

title: 1990 Colombian Constitutional Assembly election.
text: Constitutional Assembly elections were held in Colombia on 9 December 1990 alongside a referendum on the Assembly itself. The Assembly sat from February to July 1991 and drew up the 1991 constitution.

title: 5 de enero se emitió el último episodio de Amar y vivir.
text: Amar y vivir es una serie colombiana producida por Colombiana de Televisión en 1988. Original de Germán Escallón con libretos de Carlos Duplat.

El narcotráfico ha tenido directa influencia en la vida política, social y económica, del país; también como actor importante del conflicto armado interno, siendo el apoyo económico directo e indi…

title: El grupo de narcotraficantes conocidos como "Los Extraditables" le ofrecen un pacto al Presidente de Colombia, Virgilio Barco en el que aceptarían la victoria de las autoridades y cesarían sus ataques de terroristas a cambio de garantías…

title: Cumbre especial en Cartagena de Indias entre los presidentes de Colombia, Virgilio Barco, George H.W. Bush de Estados Unidos, Jaime Paz Zamora de Bolivia y Alan García del Perú con el objeto de coordinar la guerra contra las drogas.

text: César Augusto Gaviria Trujillo es un economista y político colombiano. Fue presidente de Colombia entre el 7 de agosto de 1990 y el 7 de agosto de 1994 y como secretario general de la Organización de los Estados Americanos de 1994 a 2004.​Es miembro del Partido Liberal Colombiano.

title: Inicia la participación de Colombia en la Copa Mundial de Fútbol de 1990 en Italia, tras 28 años de ausencia en el torneo con victoria 2-0 ante Emiratos Árabes Unidos disputado en Bolonia, con goles de Bernardo Redín y Carlos Valderrama…
text: La Copa Mundial de la FIFA Italia 1990 fue la decimocuarta edición de la Copa Mundial de Fútbol. Se desarrolló en Italia, entre el 8 de junio y el 8 de julio de 1990.

text: La selección de fútbol de Yugoslavia fue el equipo representativo de dicho país en las competiciones oficiales. Gestionada por la Asociación de Fútbol de Yugoslavia, era miembro de la UEFA. El equipo nacional representó, entre 1920 y 1992, a las distintas denominaciones del estado de Yugoslavia, que agrupaba a los actuales estados de Bosnia y Herzegovina, Croacia, Eslovenia, Macedonia del Norte, Montenegro, Serbia…

text: Freddy Eusebio Rincón Valencia​​ fue un futbolista y entrenador colombiano, que se desempeñó como centrocampista ofensivo o mixto. Es considerado uno de los mejores jugadores colombianos de la historia y del fútbol sudamericano en los 90.​ ​El club más importante de su trayectoria fue el Real Madrid y legado más grande fue en Corinthians donde se volvió una de las máximas leyendas de ese club.

title: Colombia es eliminada de la Copa Mundial de Fútbol de 1990 en los octavos de final contra la selección de Camerún, se recuerda el fallo de René Higuita en una salida hasta el medio campo se disputó en Nápoles.

text: N. N. es una serie de televisión colombiana producida por Colombiana de Televisión entre 1990 y 1995. N. N. fue creada y protagonizada por Germán Escallón, quien interpretaba a Nerón Navarrete, un hombre de origen campesino que busca una vida mejor en la ciudad.

title: en Cove Neck (Long Island, cerca de Nueva York) se accidenta un avión de Avianca que volaba desde Medellín (Colombia) hasta Nueva York (Estados Unidos). Mueren 73 personas. (Véase Vuelo 52 de Avianca).
text: Cover Neck es una villa ubicada en el condado de Nassau en el estado estadounidense de Nueva York. En el año 2000 tenía una población de 300 habitantes y una densidad poblacional de 90 personas por km².

Inició su vida delictiva a finales …

title: en Colombia, el cuerpo élite de la policía mata a John Jairo Arias, alias Pinina.
text: John Jairo Arias Tascón fue un sicario, jefe militar y miembro del Cartel del Medellín. Fue jefe de sicarios de Pablo Escobar, señalado por las autoridades colombianas como responsable de muchos actos criminales en Colombia entre 1984 y 1990.

title: en Colombia, el cuerpo élite de la policía mata a Gustavo Gaviria Rivero, primo de Pablo Escobar.
text: Gustavo de Jesús Gaviria Rivero, alias de El León,​​fue un narcotraficante colombiano, miembro del Cartel de Medellín. Era el segundo al mando y encargado de las finanzas de la organización delictiva, además de lugarteniente de su primo Pablo Escobar.

title: Fútbol Profesional Colombiano: América de Cali (7.ª vez).
text: La División Mayor del Fútbol Colombiano es una entidad deportiva que forma parte de la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol y se encarga de organizar, administrar y reglamentar los torneos de fútbol profesional en Colombia: Primera A; Primera B; la Copa Colombia, la Superliga de Colombia y la Liga Femenina.

text: Rodrigo D. No Futuro es una película colombiana dirigida por el cineasta antioqueño Víctor Gaviria y protagonizada por Ramiro Meneses.​​ Fue rodada en la ciudad de Medellín, Antioquia, entre 1986 y 1988. En mayo de 1990 la película debutó en el Festival de Cine de Cannes en su edición número 43.​ Narra la historia de Rodrigo, un joven que busca suplir su vacío maternal y existencial convirtiéndose en un músico de …

title: María Cano
text: María Cano es una película biográfica colombiana de 1990 dirigida por Camila Loboguerrero y protagonizada por un elenco de reconocidos actores como María Eugenia Dávila, Frank Ramírez, Diego Vélez, Maguso, Germán Escallón, Jorge Herrera y Didier Fort.

title: Amar y vivir
text: Amar y vivir es una película colombiana estrenada en 1990, dirigida por Carlos Duplat y protagonizada por María Fernanda Martínez, Luis Eduardo Motoa, Patricia Grisales, Adriana Herrán, Edgardo Román y Álvaro Rodríguez.

title: Japan launches the Hiten spacecraft, the first lunar probe launched by a country other than the Soviet Union or the United States.
text: The Hiten spacecraft, given the English name Celestial Maiden and known before launch as MUSES-A (Mu Space Engineering Spacecraft A), part of the MUSES Program, was built by the Institute of Space and Astronautical Science of Japan and launched on January 24, 1990. It was Japan's first lunar probe, the first robotic lunar probe since the Soviet Union's Luna 24 in 1976, and the first lunar probe launched by a count…

title: The Pale Blue Dot photograph of Earth is sent back from the Voyager 1 probe after completing its primary mission, from around 3.5 billion miles away.
text: Pale Blue Dot is a photograph of Earth taken on February 14, 1990, by the Voyager 1 space probe from an unprecedented distance of over 6 billion kilometers, as part of that day's Family Portrait series of images of the Solar System. In the photograph, Earth's apparent size is less than a pixel; the planet appears as a tiny dot against the vastness of space, among bands of sunlight reflected by the camera.

title: The Space Shuttle Discovery places the Hubble Space Telescope into orbit.
text: Space Shuttle Discovery is a retired American Space Shuttle orbiter. The spaceplane was one of the orbiters from NASA's Space Shuttle program and the third of five fully operational orbiters to be built.

title: Steven Balbus makes his first discovery leading to elucidation of magnetorotational instability.
text: Steven Andrew Balbus is an American astrophysicist who is the Savilian Professor of Astronomy Emeritus at the University of Oxford and a senior research fellow at New College, Oxford. In 2013, he shared the Shaw Prize for Astronomy with John F. Hawley.

title: Earth-grazing meteoroid of 13 October 1990: A 44 kilogram, 41.5 km/s meteoroid passes above Czechoslovakia and Poland at 97.9 km. It is the first time calculations of the orbit of such a body based on photographic records from two distant…
text: On 13 October 1990, meteoroid EN131090, with an estimated mass of 44 kg, entered the Earth's atmosphere above Czechoslovakia and Poland and, after a few seconds, returned to space. Observations of such events are quite rare; this was the second recorded using scientific astronomical instruments and the first recorded from two distant positions, which enabled the calculation of several of its orbital characteristics.

title: Stephen Blumberg is arrested for stealing more than 23,600 books in North America.
text: Stephen Carrie Blumberg is best known as a bibliomane who lived in Ottumwa, Iowa. After being arrested for stealing more than 23,600 books worth US$5.3 million in 1990 (equivalent to about $13M in 2025), he became known as the Book Bandit and was recognized as the most successful book thief in the history of the United States.

title: An adaptation of Anton Chekhov's play Three Sisters opens at the Gate Theatre in Dublin with locally born Sinéad, Sorcha and Niamh Cusack in the title rôles and their father Cyril Cusack as Dr. Chebutykin.
text: Anton Pavlovich Chekhov was a Russian playwright, short story writer, and physician. Widely considered one of the greatest writers of all time, his career as a playwright produced four classics, and his best short stories are held in high esteem by writers and critics.

title: Alicia Girón García is the first woman to become director of the Biblioteca Nacional de España.
text: The Biblioteca Nacional de España is the national library of Spain. It is the largest public library in the country, and one of the largest in the world.

title: J. K. Rowling has the idea for Harry Potter while on a train from Manchester to London: "I was staring out the window, and the idea for Harry just came. He appeared in my mind's eye, very fully formed. The basic idea was for a boy who…
text: Joanne Rowling, better known by her pen name J. K. Rowling, is a British author, philanthropist, producer, and screenwriter. She is best known for writing Harry Potter, a seven-volume series about a young wizard and the best-selling book series in history, with over 600 million copies sold.

title: Nicci Gerrard marries Sean French in the London Borough of Hackney, to make up a writing team known as Nicci French.
text: Nicci French is the pseudonym of English husband-and-wife team Nicci Gerrard and Sean French (born 28 May 1959), who write psychological thrillers together. The couple met in 1989 while working at the New Statesman and published their first co-written novel, The Memory Game, in 1997.

title: Uncertain date – Austrian writer Ernest Bornemann is awarded the first Magnus Hirschfeld Medal for sexual research.
text: Ernst Wilhelm Julius Bornemann, also known by his self-chosen anglicisation Ernest Borneman, was a German crime writer, filmmaker, anthropologist, ethnomusicologist, psychoanalyst, sexologist, communist agitator, jazz musician and critic. In 1988, Ernest Bornemann argued that pedophilic acts involving neither physical nor psychological violence did not necessarily have negative consequences for the child.

title: Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum theft: Twelve paintings, collectively worth from $100 to $300 million, are stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston, Massachusetts by two thieves posing as police officers. This is the…
text: In the early hours of March 18, 1990, 13 works of art were stolen from the Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum in Boston. Security guards admitted two men posing as policemen responding to a disturbance call, and the thieves bound the guards and looted the museum over the next hour.

title: Robert Mapplethorpe's "The Perfect Moment" show of nude and homosexual photographs opens at the Cincinnati Contemporary Art Centre, in spite of accusations of indecency by Citizens for Community Values.
text: Robert Michael Mapplethorpe was an American photographer and artist. Best known for his black-and-white photographs, his work encompassed celebrity portraits, self-portraits, erotic photographs, and still lifes of flowers.

title: Portrait of Doctor Gachet by Vincent van Gogh is sold for a record $82.5 million.

title: East Side Gallery, 105 paintings by 129 artists from 20 countries, is painted on the east side of the Berlin Wall in Germany following its abandonment. It includes Dmitri Vrubel's My God, Help Me to Survive This Deadly Love and Birgit…
text: The East Side Gallery memorial in Berlin-Friedrichshain is a permanent open-air gallery on the longest surviving section of the Berlin Wall in Mühlenstraße between the Berlin Ostbahnhof and the Oberbaumbrücke along the Spree. It consists of a series of murals painted directly on a 1,316 m long remnant of the Berlin Wall, located near the centre of Berlin, on Mühlenstraße in Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg.

title: John Keane is commissioned by the British Imperial War Museum as an official war artist in the Gulf War.
text: A war artist is an artist either commissioned by a government or publication, or self-motivated, to document first-hand experience of war in any form of illustrative or depictive record. War artists explore the visual and sensory dimensions of war, often absent in written histories or other accounts of warfare.
